look_here_first: E. DAVIDII vs E. DENTATA: Do NOT use leaf color, erect habit or leaf teeth alone. Examine the UNDERSIDE of a mature leaf: David's spurge generally has relatively SHORT, STIFF, STRONGLY TAPERED hairs, often arising from minute pustular bumps. Tooth-edged E. dentata generally has LONGER, WEAKER threadlike hairs. Then look at fully mature seed: David's spurge has a more ANGULAR cross section and irregular low bumps; E. dentata has smaller, ROUNDER, more evenly pebbled seeds. A fully mature capsule is generally about 4–4.8 mm wide in davidii vs 3.5–4 mm in dentata; measure with a real scale. Green three-lobed fruits and reddish leaves are shared clues, not proof. Without hairs or seed, report Euphorbia dentata–davidii group.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Euphorbia sect. Poinsettia: milky latex and cyathia; the dentata group is difficult enough that mature seed characters are often the safest species-level evidence.

key_traits.label: Growth form
key_traits.text: Annual taprooted herb, typically erect to ascending; often more robust than E. dentata but habit overlaps.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Mostly opposite, coarsely toothed, often more elliptic than E. dentata, but leaf shape overlaps too much to use alone.

key_traits.label: Hairs
key_traits.text: E. davidii shows noticeably shorter, stiffer, tapered hairs on the ABAXIAL (lower) blade, frequently with tiny enlarged bases. Under-leaf hairs are the first practical separating part from E. dentata, which has longer, slender flexible hairs.

key_traits.label: Cyathium
key_traits.text: Single yellow-green gland, broadly attached; opening oblong; appendages absent.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Capsules broadly ovoid, about 2.9–3.3 × 4–4.8 mm, 3-lobed and usually glabrous; larger than in E. dentata.

key_traits.label: Seed
key_traits.text: Dry mature seed 2.4–2.9 × 2.2–2.9 mm (FNA), angular cross section and irregularly clustered wartlike protuberances, contrasted with dentata smaller more rounded seed and more even fine bumps. Photograph at two rotational angles with 1 mm scale.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Annual from taproot; tall or ascending, repeatedly branching, especially in disturbed open soil. Habit is variable and not species-specific.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Coarsely crenate-toothed leaves, frequently opposite, sometimes alternate higher in the plant; leaf blade shape and red/purple margin not reliable alone.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Some stems and leaf edges visibly hairy; key microscopic species feature is short, STIFF, strongly tapered hairs on the LEAF UNDERSIDE.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Short abaxial hair bases are often MINUTELY PUSTULAR; a second sharply focused macro is essential to truly see their bases.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Terminal small green cyathia and three-lobed fruiting capsules; one main yellow-green gland of oblong opening without petal-like appendages (must be a real macro to label).

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Capsules glabrous or scarcely hairy, 2.9–3.3 mm high and 4–4.8 mm across in FNA. Need a scale; young fruits don't reliably match dimensions.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Mature seeds approximately 2.4–2.9 × 2.2–2.9 mm; angular in cross section with irregular/faintly transverse low wartlike bumps.

lookalikes.differences: E. davidii = stiff short hairs + larger capsule + larger angular irregularly lumpy seed. E. dentata = longer weak filiform hairs + smaller capsule + smaller rounded evenly finely tuberculate seed.
